rules:
- A CABIN has no backup cabin assigned if there is no incoming BACKUP_FOR relationship to it; check for existence using NOT EXISTS { (:CABIN)-[:BACKUP_FOR]->(c) }.
- When connecting ONT to OLT, traverse the CONNECTS_TO relationship in the forward direction (ONT → … → OLT) using hop counts 5..6, and ensure this path is matched separately from the OLT–SITE connection using a second MATCH clause before aggregating.
- When traversing from an ONT to a SPLITTER, use the pattern (:ONT)-[:CONNECTS_TO*1..2]->(:SPLITTER) — the relationship always points *from* ONT *to* SPLITTER.
- Do not assume direct CONNECTS_TO relationships between ONT and SPLITTER; instead, use variable-length path [:CONNECTS_TO*1..2] to match all valid ONT-to-SPLITTER connections.
- Return a unique identifying property of the target node instead of the full path.
- Do not use the BACKUP_FOR relationship to exclude CABIN nodes when counting ONTs per CABIN; instead, connect CABIN -[:CONNECTS_TO]-> SPLITTER and count ONTs via ONT -[:CONNECTS_TO*1..2]-> SPLITTER directly.
- Do not exclude paths to PORT nodes on the basis of intermediate SPLITTER nodes when searching upstream from an ONT, because ONTs commonly connect through SPLITTERS to reach their upstream PORTs.
- ONT nodes connect directly to either SPLITTER or SUB_SPLITTER via CONNECTS_TO, and SUB_SPLITTER nodes connect to SPLITTER via CONNECTS_TO, so to find ONTs served by a SPLITTER (directly or via sub-splitter), traverse CONNECTS_TO relationships for 1 to 2 hops from the SPLITTER to reach the ONT.
- When traversing from a splitter to an OLT in this schema, use CONNECTS_TO*4 (not from OLT back to splitter), and ensure ONTs are connected *to* splitters via CONNECTS_TO*1..2 or CONNECTS_TO — do not start from SITE and traverse toward ONTs through OLT using reverse relationships; instead, start from SPLITTER, go to OLT via CONNECTS_TO*4, then to SITE via IN_SITE, and finally collect ONTs connected to the splitter.
- From SPLITTER, traverse forward along CONNECTS_TO*4 to reach OLT, and from ONT, traverse forward along CONNECTS_TO*1..2 to reach SPLITTER; do not reverse the direction of CONNECTS_TO when matching the schema’s defined path directions.
- Do not assume ONTs connect through OLTs; ONTs connect directly to SPLITTERs or SUB_SPLITTERs via CONNECTS_TO, and CABINs connect directly to SPLITTERs via CONNECTS_TO.
- CARD nodes do not have an IN_SITE relationship with SITE nodes; instead, CARD nodes connect directly to OLT nodes via CONNECTS_TO.
- When counting ports per card, match ports that connect *to* the card using (:PORT)-[:CONNECTS_TO]->(:CARD), not the reverse.
- Match ONT nodes using the exact lowercase value "faulty" for the status property directly in the node pattern, not "FAULTY", and use DISTINCT to avoid duplicate counts across variable-length paths.
- When counting ONTs by status under a specific OLT, match ONT to OLT directly via [:CONNECTS_TO*5..6], not through intermediate CABIN or SPLITTER nodes, because ONTs connect to OLTs in 5–6 hops per the schema.
- Do not assume :SPLITTER connects directly to :SITE; instead, use the path (:SPLITTER)-[:CONNECTS_TO*4]->(:OLT)-[:IN_SITE]->(:SITE) to reach a site.
